sub_branches.concept: Suraj's Exploration & The Steam Engine Metaphor
details: Young Suraj cycles out of town, leaves his bicycle at a scrub village, and walks to a deep forest railway cutting.
Waits at the horseshoe masonry arch not to ride the train, but to experience its sensory arrival.
Views the steam locomotive as a magnificent 'green, black, and gold dragon, snorting and puffing, showering sparks'.
Demonstrates pure childhood adventure, wonder, and fascination with heavy machinery.
evidence_or_examples: Suraj standing on the high embankment watching steam plumes burst from the tunnel.

details: Sunder Singh is the solitary railway watchman living in a small hut near the cutting.
Walks the entire length of the dark tunnel before every train to inspect tracks for rockfalls or animals.
Maintains strict safety protocols: green flag/lamp for clear tracks, red flag/lamp for danger.
Views his job as a solemn responsibility to protect human lives and forest wildlife.
evidence_or_examples: Sunder Singh carrying his oil lamp, red flag, and axe into the dark tunnel.

details: A wild leopard uses the dark tunnel as its shelter during hot days.
Sunder Singh explains that the leopard knows him well and preys on stray goats rather than humans.
When the night mail train approaches at 9 p.m., Sunder Singh enters the tunnel with his axe and lamp.
Shouts and makes noise to drive the leopard safely into the surrounding brush before the train roars through.
evidence_or_examples: Driving the leopard off the tracks so it will not be struck and killed by the night mail.

details: Suraj later boards the night train with his family and looks back into the dark cutting.
Sees Sunder Singh holding his glowing oil lamp—a solitary 'firefly' lighting up the forest night.
Symbolizes how small, humble human acts of duty illuminate vast darkness.
Grammar Focus: Use of 'would' + base verb to express habitual past actions (e.g., 'Sunder Singh would walk the tunnel').
evidence_or_examples: Suraj seeing the small yellow light of Sunder Singh's lamp receding in the dark jungle.

branches.theme: Reflective Poem: Travel by Edna St. Vincent Millay

sub_branches.concept: Wanderlust & The Universal Call of Exploration
details: Expresses an inescapable, deep-seated longing to travel and see distant places.
Regardless of daily human warmth, quiet conversations, or comfortable surroundings, the speaker's mind drifts.
Hearing a distant train whistle at night immediately triggers intense wanderlust.
Uses auditory imagery ('whistle shrieking') and visual imagery ('cinders red on the sky') to capture the romance of railways.
evidence_or_examples: The speaker stating that no matter what friends are speaking during the day, night train whistles compel her thoughts.
